name: Alcove
description:
Alcove turns the MacBook notch into an interactive, Dynamic Island-style surface. Instead of leaving that part of the display as unused hardware, it presents animated status, controls, and quick information when you hover or interact with the area.

The value is mostly in making common background activity more glanceable. Media playback, system HUDs, charging state, notifications, calendar information, and lock-screen widgets can appear where the eye already goes, rather than taking over the desktop with another panel.

Alcove is designed around polish and restraint rather than filling the notch with every possible module. It aims to feel integrated with macOS, giving MacBook owners a small interaction surface that is visible when useful and quiet when it is not.

## Features

- Display live activities and instant notifications through an animated notch interaction inspired by the iPhone Dynamic Island.
- Show media controls and playback information near the notch so common listening actions remain easy to reach.
- Surface customizable system HUDs for states such as volume, brightness, battery, and charging.
- Integrate current Focus mode, calendar, and Lock Screen widget capabilities where permission and the installed release support them.
- Use swipe gestures and hover interactions to open, dismiss, or move through notch content without adding a permanent desktop panel.
- Access Alcove as a native Mac utility with a visual style intentionally focused on fluid transitions and small, contained interactions.

## Where it fits

Alcove is best for MacBook users who want the notch to provide subtle media, status, and calendar utility without installing a more expansive widget dashboard. It is most attractive when visual integration and restrained behavior matter as much as feature count.

It is not essential on a Mac without a notch, and its value is inherently personal. Users seeking file shelves, clipboard history, or dense productivity modules may prefer a broader notch utility.
